versions.short: The bill would create a task force or similar program within the Criminal Division of the Department of Justice to investigate and prosecute trade-related crimes, such as evading tariffs and duties, smuggling, trade-based money laundering, and certain fraud and health or safety violations tied to imports and exports. It would add new prosecutor and support positions, require training and coordination with agencies like Homeland Security Investigations and U.S. Customs and Border Protection, and allow the Department to work with foreign trading partners. The Attorney General would also have to report annually to Congress on trade-crime cases, spending, and any additional funding needed.
